summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease and severe peripheral vascular disease was admitted for a right below-the-knee amputation due to unrelenting pain and tissue necrosis from ischemia. Postoperatively, she developed cellulitis at the stump site, managed with intravenous antibiotics including vancomycin, ciprofloxacin, and metronidazole. Phantom limb pain was initially severe but improved with a ketamine drip and transition to oral analgesics. A second procedure was performed to place stents in the left superficial femoral artery and perform angioplasty on the right common iliac artery to improve circulation. Her anticoagulation was managed with a heparin drip while warfarin was restarted, though her INR remained subtherapeutic at discharge. She participated in physical therapy, was weaned off narcotics, and was discharged to extended care with plans for wound care, anticoagulation monitoring, and gradual tapering of oxycodone.
